title: As our seeing does not change what we see, God's foresight changes nothing in future things
source_text: XXV. Itaque necesse est quidem omnia illa fieri, quae Deus futura praevidet, supposita semel ista praevisione: quemadmodum necesse est fieri omnia illa, quae nos ipsi fieri videmus, supposita nostra visione. Sed sicut visio nostra non mutat naturam rerum, nec facit ut in se necessarium sit, quod ex sua natura liberum, sive contingens est: quamvis ex hypothesi quod aliquid fieri videmus, non possit illud non esse: sic praevisio Dei nihil immutat in rebus futuris, nec earum libertatem, aut contingentiam tollit: quamvis illud quod futurum a Deo praevidetur, & sic supponitur futurum, non possit non esse futurum. Nam sicut ex hypothesi quod res actu sit, impossibile est eam non esse actu, eodem plane modo ex hypothesi quod res futura sit, fieri non potest ut non sit futura.
pass_a_gloss: XXV. Therefore it is necessary indeed that all those things be done, which God foresees as future, that foresight being once supposed: just as it is necessary that all those things be done, which we ourselves see being done, our sight being supposed. But just as our sight does not change the nature of things, nor makes that to be necessary in itself, which from its own nature is free, or contingent: although from the hypothesis that we see something being done, it cannot not be: so the foresight of God changes nothing in future things, nor takes away their liberty, or contingency: although that which is foreseen by God as future, and so is supposed future, cannot not be future. For just as from the hypothesis that a thing actually is, it is impossible that it not actually be, in plainly the same way from the hypothesis that a thing is future, it cannot be that it should not be future.
pass_b_english: Once God's foresight is supposed, then, everything he foresees as future must indeed happen. In the same way, once our own seeing is supposed, everything we see happening must be happening.

Our seeing does not alter the nature of things. It does not make something necessary in itself that is free or contingent by its own nature, even though, given that we see it happening, it cannot fail to be. In just the same way God's foresight alters nothing in future things and does not take away their freedom or contingency. This holds even though what God foresees as future, being supposed future, cannot fail to be future.
If we suppose that a thing actually exists, it cannot fail to exist actually. In exactly the same way, if we suppose that a thing is future, it cannot fail to be future.

lemmas.latin: visio nostra non mutat naturam rerum
lemmas.gloss: our sight does not change the nature of things

choices.why: The standard English term for God's knowing in advance; 'foreknowledge' is kept throughout for praescientia, with 'foresee' for praevidere.
